title: Integral closure commutes with ind-etale base change
statement: Let $R,B,S$ be commutative rings equipped with ring maps $R\to B$ and $R\to S$. Assume $R\to S$ is ind-etale, meaning that $S$ is a filtered colimit of finitely presented etale $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $C\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $B$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Equip $S\otimes_R B$ with its tensor-product algebra structure, $(s\otimes b)(s^{\prime}\otimes b^{\prime})=ss^{\prime}\otimes bb^{\prime}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and let $C_S\subseteq S\otimes_R B$ be the integral closure of $S$ in this algebra. The canonical $S$-algebra map $S\otimes_R C\longrightarrow C_S$, $s\otimes c\longmapsto s\otimes c$, is an isomorphism. No injectivity, domain, Noetherian, finiteness, nonemptiness, or local-ring assumption on these rings is required.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth: specialization from a filtered colimit of smooth algebras to a filtered colimit of etale algebras.

proof.text: Choose a filtered presentation of $S$ by finitely presented etale $R$-algebras using [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal], reindex it by a nonempty directed set $I$, retaining $S$ and its coprojections $a_i:S_i\to S$ as the colimit in commutative $R$-algebras. Choose a common ambient universe for the diagram and its algebra carriers. Put $D_i=S_i\otimes_R B$, $E_i=S_i\otimes_R C$, $D=S\otimes_R B$, and $E=S\otimes_R C$. For every transition $u:i\le j$ use $a_u\otimes1$ on these tensor products. By [lem-sfb-integral-closure-etale-base-change], $q_i:E_i\to\overline{S_i}^{\,D_i}$ is an isomorphism, with $q_i(s\otimes c)=s\otimes c$. Denote its composite with the subring inclusion by $f_i:E_i\to D_i$; in particular $f_i$ is injective. All the rings $R,B,S_i$ satisfy that leaf's hypotheses, without hypotheses on the transition maps.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth, proof; finite-stage case Tag 03GE, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-etale.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise], applied with $N=C$ and $N=B$, every element of $E$ or $D$ lifts to a stage; an element at a stage mapping to zero is zero after a later transition. The stage-to-limit and transition maps are ring maps. The tensor map $f:E\to D$ induced by $C\subseteq B$ commutes with them: on $s\otimes c$ both composites give $a_i(s)\otimes c$, and pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For $t\in E$, lift it to $t_i\in E_i$. The element $f_i(t_i)$ is integral over $S_i$ by step 1. Map its monic annihilating polynomial coefficientwise along $a_i$; the resulting monic polynomial over $S$ annihilates $f(t)$ because ring maps preserve sums and products [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Thus $f$ lands in $C_S$ and defines the required $S$-algebra map $q:E\to C_S$. Its pure-tensor formula is the one in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth, proof; finite-stage case Tag 03GE, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-etale.

proof.text: If $q(t)=0$, lift $t$ to $t_i\in E_i$. Then $f_i(t_i)$ maps to zero in $D$. The eventual-zero clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] for $N=B$ gives $u:i\le j$ with $(a_u\otimes1)f_i(t_i)=0$. By the pure-tensor compatibility this is $f_j((a_u\otimes1)t_i)=0$. The injectivity of $f_j$ from step 1 gives $(a_u\otimes1)t_i=0$; its image in $E$ is $t$, so $t=0$. Applying this to a difference proves that $q$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth, proof; finite-stage case Tag 03GE, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-etale.

proof.text: Let $x\in C_S$ and lift its underlying element to $x_i\in D_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] with $N=B$. For any $S_i$-algebra $T$ obtained from $S_j$ ($j\ge i$) or $S$, the maps $T\otimes_{S_i}(S_i\otimes_R B)\to T\otimes_R B$, $t\otimes(s\otimes b)\mapsto ts\otimes b$, and $t\otimes b\mapsto t\otimes(1\otimes b)$ are mutually inverse: balancing moves $s$ to the first factor, and the formulas preserve multiplication and units. Likewise $T\otimes_{S_i}S_i\cong T$ via $t\otimes s\mapsto ts$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Under these identifications $1\otimes x_i$ over $S$ is $x$. Restrict the directed system to indices $j\ge i$; it still has colimit $S$, since every index has a common upper bound with $i$, and any compatible cocone on the tail extends uniquely by those upper bounds. The colimit is also one in commutative rings: a cocone of commutative rings $(T,(b_j)_{j\ge i})$ on the tail becomes a cocone of commutative $R$-algebras when $T$ is given the structure map $b_j\circ(R\to S_j)$, which is independent of $j$ because the transition maps are $R$-algebra maps and any two indices have a common upper bound; the induced $R$-algebra map $S\to T$ is the unique ring map compatible with the $b_j$, since such a map is automatically $R$-linear for this structure. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-tensor-generators-colimit-descent] with initial index $i$, $B_0=S_i$, $C_0=D_i$, the structure map $S_i\to D_i$, and the singleton $\{x_i\}$. Its integrality hypothesis is exactly $x\in C_S$. It gives $j\ge i$ for which the image $x_j$ of $x_i$ in $D_j$ is integral over $S_j$.

source.place: Tag 0CBF, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-colim-smooth, proof; finite-stage case Tag 03GE, lemma-integral-closure-commutes-etale.

proof.text: By the finite-stage isomorphism $q_j$ in step 1, there exists $t_j\in E_j$ with $f_j(t_j)=x_j$. Its image $t$ in $E$ satisfies $q(t)=x$: their underlying elements in $D$ agree by the compatibility checked in step 2, and the inclusion $C_S\subseteq D$ is injective. This proves surjectivity. Together with step 3, $q$ is a bijective $S$-algebra homomorphism, hence an isomorphism (its inverse preserves operations by applying the injective map $q$). Zero rings cause no exception, and the nonempty index used above comes from filteredness, not from a hypothesis that a ring is nonzero.
